panels.note: Under all that guilt, he just wants to come home. Seeing him finally say it makes this so much more emotional than any fight.

panels.title: Franky defeats Señor Pink

panels.note: Fifty years of loneliness, and he finally has people to laugh with again. A skeleton saying he is happy to be alive should not hurt this much.

panels.note: Calling an Emperor a young lady while standing right in front of her is insane. Brook’s calm confidence here is so good.
panels.title: Brook stands against Big Mom

panels.note: After an entire arc about prejudice, sharing blood says so much without needing another battle. One of the most beautiful Jinbe moments.
panels.title: Jinbe gives his blood to Luffy

panels.note: He knows exactly who he wants to sail with. Standing this calmly in front of Big Mom makes his faith in Luffy feel unshakable.
panels.title: Jinbe faces Big Mom without fear

panels.note: Five feet on a barrel, five dreams, and the whole sea ahead of them. This is the feeling of adventure I love about One Piece.
panels.title: The East Blue five share their dreams / Usopp’s vow

panels.note: They cannot call out to her, so they answer with their arms raised. No speech needed. Such a beautiful goodbye.

panels.note: Oda really made a ship feel like a friend we were losing. The apology, the snow, everyone crying. This one destroys me.
panels.title: Going Merry’s funeral

panels.note: The story opens with an ending that sends the whole world out to sea. Such a perfect beginning for an adventure this huge.

panels.note: A dream dismissed as a lie finally reaches the people waiting below. That giant shadow in the sky is such a beautiful payoff.
panels.title: Shandora’s bell rings / Luffy’s shadow over Jaya

panels.note: After all that fighting to save him, this quiet goodbye is unbearable. The relief on his face makes it hurt even more.

panels.note: Even at the end, he makes sure the world has to listen. The scale of this moment feels bigger than the battlefield.

After many years, this is how Sei encounters his mother following her abandonment of him in court long ago. He feels fear, and although she has aged, he still perceives her as the younger woman he once feared.
His mom’s backstory and after all of that evil stuff she did writer still made me sad for her and hoping that Sei take care of her.

This is the final panel. Grudges may endure for years, yet even the harshest ones tend to fade as time passes. Sei arrived too late for healing; his trauma resolved only after he grew much older, much like his mother. The man who once enjoyed her was dead, having spent his life hating her for what she did; now the story ends with Sei unable to recall the face of the mother he once despised and wasted his life on. If you fail to move on while carrying trauma, time shifts, emotions alter, and everything changes—you remain the only person unchanged or unmoved, trapped in a time paradox. Once you exit the bubble, you wonder why you were ever like this in the first place.
